11.text: a family, even a young child, has a dream about sports, such sports must be

18.text: The thanksgiving ceremonial must have a central object. On most oc-

19.text: casions it is a reindeer, wolverene, thong-seal, or other animal killed in hunting.

20.text: Native or foreign objects of trade — a dried seal-skin, a cake of tea, or a

21.text: bundle of tobacco — may, however, serve the purpose. The Reindeer Chuk-

22.text: chee often slaughter a reindeer of their own herd, and perform the ceremo-

24.text: The ceremonial is performed indoors. Not even a fire is built outside of

25.text: the tent. The object of the ceremonial is placed on a skin by the side of

26.text: the fire on the hearth. A large quantity of fat meat is boiled, and the sacri-

27.text: ficial blood-soup is prepared with fat and roots. The people gathered for the

28.text: ceremonial partake of the food, while the children of the family carry plates

29.text: containing meat around the outside of the tent, in the direction of the course

30.text: of the sun. The principal heir, boy or girl,¹ walks ahead; and all the par-

31.text: ticipants shout at the top of the voice, “Yoho, yoho!” which is intended

32.text: to drive away the evil spirits. After that, the young people scatter the sacri-

33.text: fice to all “directions” in the usual way, and bury some pieces of it in the

34.text: earth. Meanwhile the women climb to the top of the tent, and carefully

35.text: cover the vent-hole with skins. The fire on the hearth is kept low, never-

36.text: theless the tent is full of smoke during the whole performance. The entrance

37.text: is left open. Then the mistress of the house takes a drum and goes about

38.text: inside beating it, for the purpose of frightening away the “spirits.” When all

39.text: the “spirits” are supposed to have flown away through the entrance, and the

40.text: young people who went out with the sacrifice have returned, the door is closed.
